chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 03 (Unit 13 & 14: Support, Movement & Reproduction)
subject: biology-10

questions.question: The total number of bones present in an adult human skeleton is: (FBISE Annual 2024)
questions.explanation: The adult human skeletal framework comprises 206 bones, divided into the axial (80) and appendicular (126) skeletons.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an immovable fibrous joint in the human skeleton? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Cranial sutures are immovable synarthrodial fibrous joints that lock adjacent skull plates securely together.

questions.question: The tough band of fibrous connective tissue connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone is called a: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Tendons connect contractile muscles to bones, while ligaments connect bones together at joint articulations.

questions.question: In the human arm, which muscle acts as an extensor to straighten the arm at the elbow joint?
questions.explanation: The triceps brachii contracts to pull on the ulna, extending and straightening the forearm at the elbow.

questions.question: A systemic bone disease characterized by porous, brittle bones due to loss of calcium salts is: (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis involves diminished bone mineral density and deterioration of microarchitecture, increasing fracture risk.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction in bread mold (Rhizopus) occurs predominantly by the formation of: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Rhizopus reproduces asexually through airborne non-motile spores developed inside bulbous terminal sporangia.

questions.question: In honeybees, the parthenogenetic development of unfertilized eggs produces: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Male drone honeybees develop parthenogenetically from unfertilized haploid eggs, whereas fertilized diploid eggs produce females.

questions.question: Which of the following plants propagates vegetatively through underground modified stems called rhizomes?
questions.explanation: Ginger develops underground horizontal stems known as rhizomes, bearing nodes, internodes, and adventitious buds.

questions.question: Double fertilization in angiosperm flowers yields which two vital structures? (FBISE 2024)

options.B: A diploid zygote (2n) and a triploid endosperm nucleus (3n)
options.C: A haploid spore and a seed coat

questions.explanation: One sperm fuses with the egg cell (2n zygote), while the second sperm fuses with two polar nuclei to yield 3n endosperm.

questions.question: In epigeal seed germination (e.g., in bean seeds), which part elongates rapidly to pull cotyledons above the soil?
questions.explanation: During epigeal germination, elongation of the hypocotyl arches upward and pulls the cotyledons above the ground.

questions.question: The pathogen responsible for Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: HIV is a retrovirus that attacks human CD4+ helper T-lymphocytes, destroying cell-mediated immunity.

questions.question: Which embryonic structure of a plant seed gives rise to the primary root system?
questions.explanation: The radicle is the embryonic root that emerges first through the seed coat to establish subterranean anchorage.
